title: Start mining a small body or Others mothership wreck with a Manny
description: Pick objectId from a detailed SectorObject.id or from a solar system minableTargets entry. Select resources from resourceTypes. For asteroids and Others mothership wrecks, resourceAmounts is the authoritative remaining reserve in equivalent earth containers; resourceComposition/resourceProfile define how a multi-resource targetAmount is split. An idle Manny in another sector covered by the same SCUT network can receive this order for its own sector only when targetContainerId identifies a detached container in that Manny sector.

parameters.name: probeId
parameters.description: Owned probe id. When it is not the player's default probe, the default probe and this probe must be in the same sector or in sectors covered by the same active SCUT network.

resource.description: Legacy single resource selector. Prefer resources.

targetAmount.description: Amount to mine in equivalent earth containers. Manny cargo capacity is 0.05 per trip. For deuterium-only mining, 0.01 ECE becomes 1 point in the probe tank.

targetContainerId.description: Optional detached storage container object id in the task sector. When omitted, mined resources are delivered to the probe, which is allowed only for a Manny operating in the probe sector. Remote same-SCUT mining requires this field and the referenced container must be detached in the Manny sector. When it targets a visible drifting container or a hidden container on another asteroid, normal mining travel time still applies. When it targets a hidden container on the asteroid being mined, travel time is deducted and only extraction time remains. If the container has less free capacity than targetAmount, the task is capped to its free capacity. Detached storage containers cannot receive deuterium, which remains reserved for the probe external tank.

title: Install a deuterium engine on an asteroid
description: Requires the Distributed Thrust Anchoring blueprint and an idle onboard Manny. The target asteroid must be in the selected probe sector. One deuterium engine, four steel bars, two steel plates and 0.2 deuterium point are consumed when the task starts. The task lasts one configured Manny mining outbound trip plus five minutes. On completion the asteroid receives a new opaque id, is persisted with `motorized: true` and `motorFuelStatus: full`, retains its resources and remains mineable. The Manny then automatically starts a returning task toward the probe.

title: Refuel an empty motorized asteroid

title: Sculpt an asteroid into the shape of a duck
description: Requires the Anatiform Asteroid Sculpting blueprint and an idle onboard Manny. The target must be a local asteroid that has not already been sculpted. The task takes exactly 172800 seconds (two days). The asteroid remains unchanged until completion, so cancelling or recalling the Manny before the deadline leaves it as an ordinary asteroid. On completion the asteroid gains `distinctiveFeature: Sculpted in the shape of a duck` while retaining its resources, propulsion, fuel status, trajectory compatibility and all ordinary asteroid gameplay properties. The Manny then automatically returns to the probe.

title: Launch a full motorized asteroid
description: Consumes the asteroid's binary fuel tank and creates one durable, scheduler-driven trajectory. A system impact accelerates around the sector reference star before a ten-minute coasting phase. A sector transfer accepts only a direct FCC-grid neighbor expressed in the player's relative frame; that neighbor sets a straight-line direction, and the asteroid then crosses one sector every 24 hours. Capture is guaranteed in the first entered sector containing at least one eligible body. In a stellar system the captor is selected proportionally to mass, so the star is overwhelmingly favored and places the asteroid in orbit when selected. Each sector crossed without an eligible body, and each failed capture attempt, reduces the next capture probability by 10 percentage points (100%, 90%, 80%, and so on). Crossing several empty sectors therefore makes a later capture progressively less certain. Black holes always capture the asteroid. Starting either trajectory mode interrupts every Manny mining into a container attached to the asteroid, including Mannys belonging to another probe, and sends them back with reason `target_container_departed_with_asteroid`. Absolute coordinates are never returned.

parameters.description: Owned probe id. When it is not the player's default probe, the default probe and this probe must be in the same sector or in sectors covered by the same active SCUT network.

parameters.description: Opaque id of a local full motorized asteroid.

title: Assemble a new drone probe with a Manny
description: Starts a three-hour exterior Manny task. The generic model consumes two selected empty additional containers plus one deuterium engine, one SCUT relay, five electric motors, two atomic printer parts, and four solar panels. The `deuterium_tanker` model additionally consumes ten steel plates, two linear actuators, and one integrated circuit. When the task completes, a new owned drone probe is created in the assembly sector and the Manny is transferred from the old probe to the new one. If the original probe leaves the sector before completion, the exterior Manny can be left behind as a forgotten Manny. If the task is cancelled by recall, consumed assembly ingredients are left as drifting item stacks in the assembly sector.

title: Recover a drifting sector object with a Manny
description: Starts a five-minute recovery task. Recoverable targets include abandoned Mannys, drifting item stacks, detached storage containers, and inactive SCUT relays present in the probe current sector. The target is checked again when the delay ends; if another player has already recovered it or an inactive relay has been switched on, the task completes with a failed result and no object is transferred.

Visible detached storage containers are also recoverable and keep their hidden contents out of sector observations. For item stacks, a Manny reserves at most one cargo trip of items.

title: Detach an additional storage container
description: Starts a detaching_storage_container task on an idle onboard Manny. The target must be an additional storage container, never probe-core. A container with space reserved for an active crafting output cannot be detached; the API returns `409 storage_container_reserved`. The container, its stored resources/items, and routing rules are removed from the probe inventory when the order is accepted. On completion it becomes either a visible drifting detached container, a hidden container attached to an asteroid, or a container attached to another owned probe in the same sector. Hidden-asteroid detaches expose artificialObjectDetected in the Manny task/result so clients can immediately reference the hidden detached container id.

title: Drop an additional storage container on a planet
description: Starts a dropping_storage_container task on an idle onboard Manny. The target must be a planet in the current sector and the probe inventory must contain one atmospheric_drop_kit. A container with space reserved for an active crafting output cannot be dropped; the API returns `409 storage_container_reserved`. The container, its stored resources/items, and routing rules are removed from the probe inventory when the order is accepted, and the drop kit is consumed. On completion the detached container is stored in sector JSON as attached to the planet with the origin probe id, but planet-dropped containers are not exposed by sector observation endpoints yet. If the container contains biological_archive items for an active Oracle mission, their delivery count is recorded on the owning player's mission, independently of the probe used. The destination must differ from the requesting planet and have a habitability score strictly above the configured Oracle threshold; otherwise the mission fails. After both archives are delivered, returning any probe owned by that player to the requesting sector completes the mission and creates a planet-originated message announcing the future once-per-24-hours Oracle service.

parameters.name: probeId
parameters.description: Owned probe id. When it is not the player's default probe, the default probe and this probe must be in the same sector or in sectors covered by the same active SCUT network.

title: Inspect a sector object with a Manny
description: Sends an idle Manny to an inspectable sector object without mining. Local Mannys inspect objects in the probe current sector; an idle remote Manny can also be ordered when its sector and the probe sector are covered by the same SCUT network, in which case the target object must be in the Manny sector and the Manny remains there after completion. Asteroids keep the existing hidden-detached-container detection behavior. Visible detached containers and discovered hidden detached containers generate a Manny report alert when the task completes. Dormant constructs generate a Manny report alert and unlock one probe improvement for the inspecting probe. The construct's selected recovery scenario is stored in sector data and is not exposed by the API.

parameters.name: probeId
parameters.description: Owned probe id. When it is not the player's default probe, the default probe and this probe must be in the same sector or in sectors covered by the same active SCUT network.

description: Starts a salvage-duration recovery task for a detached storage container. Drifting containers can also be recovered through the salvage endpoint. Hidden containers are recovered by the object id returned from mining or inspect-sector-object detection. Any other Mannys currently mining into the recovered detached container are interrupted across all probes, have their current mining cargo dropped, and switch to a returning task with reason `target_container_recovered`.

The Manny consumes one bookmark item when the order is accepted, spends 10 seconds giving it the needed impulse, then the normal waypoint bookmark persistence is applied to the target object.

title: Recall an exterior Manny to the probe
description: Cancels the current exterior task and starts a returning task when the Manny is outside the probe. By default the return lasts one Manny travel time. If the cancelled task has been running for less than that travel time, the Manny turns around and the return duration matches the elapsed task time. Cancelling a probe assembly task leaves its consumed ingredients as drifting item stacks in the assembly sector. When the Manny is in a different sector that shares SCUT network coverage with the probe sector, the order is accepted remotely: the task is cancelled, the Manny stays in that sector, and it is registered there as forgotten instead of returning.

parameters.name: probeId

Recoverable cargo objects, such as a salvaged Manny, drifting item, or detached storage container, are restored to the current sector as drifting/recoverable objects.

title: Transfer deuterium to another probe or drone with a Manny
description: Starts a five-minute Manny task that transfers a reserved deuterium amount from the current probe to another probe in the same sector. Neither probe may have an active movement. The requested amount must be strictly lower than the source probe current deuterium reserve. When the task completes, the target probe is filled only up to its maximum deuterium capacity and any surplus is returned to the source probe.

parameters.name: probeId
parameters.description: Owned probe id. When it is not the player's default probe, the default probe and this probe must be in the same sector or in sectors covered by the same active SCUT network.

targetProbeId.description: Target probe id. The target must be in the same sector as the source probe.

amount.description: Deuterium percentage points to reserve from the source probe and transfer after five minutes. Must be strictly lower than the source probe current deuterium reserve.

title: Transfer a Manny to another owned probe
description: Starts a Manny transfer task using the same duration as storage container detachment. The target probe must be owned by the player and in the Manny sector. The transfer is accepted when source probe, target probe, and Manny are all in the same sector, or when the Manny is in a remote SCUT-reachable sector with the target probe. If the Manny was already executing a task, the task is cancelled with the same cleanup rules as recall, then the Manny returns toward the target probe. Neither the source nor target probe may have an active movement.

parameters.name: probeId
parameters.description: Owned probe id. When it is not the player's default probe, the default probe and this probe must be in the same sector or in sectors covered by the same active SCUT network.

targetProbeId.description: Target owned probe id. The target must be in the Manny sector.

title: Send a Manny to turn on a SCUT relay
description: Starts a five-minute Manny task that turns on an inactive SCUT relay in the probe current sector. The current sector must contain a star because the relay needs solar energy. The task consumes one integrated_circuit from the probe inventory. If the relay joins existing relay coverage, the resulting network keeps the name of the largest existing network, with oldest network as tie-breaker; otherwise networkName or "scut network" is used.

parameters.name: probeId
parameters.description: Owned probe id. When it is not the player's default probe, the default probe and this probe must be in the same sector or in sectors covered by the same active SCUT network.

relayId.description: Id of an inactive SCUT relay in the probe current sector.

networkName.description: Optional name for a newly isolated network. Ignored when the relay joins existing coverage.

title: Send a Manny to install a SCUT transit beacon
description: Starts a five-minute Manny task that equips an active SCUT relay in the probe current sector with a scut_transit_beacon. The task consumes one scut_transit_beacon item from the probe inventory.

parameters.name: probeId
parameters.description: Owned probe id. When it is not the player's default probe, the default probe and this probe must be in the same sector or in sectors covered by the same active SCUT network.

relayId.description: Id of an active SCUT relay in the probe current sector.

title: Observe a sector by player-relative coordinates
description: Coordinates are relative to the authenticated player's home sector. Absolute sector coordinates are never exposed. Detail depends on whether the sector is current, visited, or only passively scanned from a reachable probe. When another owned probe is reachable from the default probe and is closer to the requested sector, its scan is used if it has enough sensor data. `sector.distance` is measured from the default probe; `sector.distances` lists the distance from every owned probe and marks the probe whose sensors produced the scan. During blind cruise, only already visited sectors can be consulted as historical cartography. This endpoint uses owned probes exclusively; Others fleet scans are exposed by `GET /api/others/sector`.

title: Send a message to a reachable probe or inhabited planet
description: Creates an unread message from the current probe to a recipient. Probe recipients must be in the exact same sector as the sender probe, or both probes must be inside coverage of the same active SCUT relay network. Planet recipients must be inhabited planets in the current sector. If the recipient type is omitted, `probe` is used. After completing an Oracle mission, sending a player's exact username to the Oracle planet whose mission has been completed by any player produces a planet-originated reply containing the approximate normalized direction vector and FCC distance to that player's default probe. A successful lookup starts a 24-hour cooldown shared by every visitor to that Oracle planet; unknown usernames do not consume it, while requests during the cooldown receive a polite refusal.

parameters.name: probeId
parameters.description: Owned probe id. When it is not the player's default probe, the default probe and this probe must be in the same sector or in sectors covered by the same active SCUT network.

schema.description: Provide `recipient`, or alternatively `recipientId` with optional `recipientType`. If no type is provided, `probe` is used.

id.description: Probe id for `probe`, planet object id for `planet`.

recipientId.description: Alternative recipient id. Used with `recipientType` or default `probe`.

recipientType.description: Alternative recipient type for clients that do not send `recipient`.

recipientProbeId.description: Legacy shortcut for `recipient: { type: probe, id: ... }`.

recipientPlanetId.description: Legacy shortcut for `recipient: { type: planet, id: ... }`.

title: Mark a received probe message as read
description: Only the recipient probe can mark a message as read. Repeating the call on an already-read message is safe and returns the message unchanged.

parameters.name: probeId
parameters.description: Owned probe id. When it is not the player's default probe, the default probe and this probe must be in the same sector or in sectors covered by the same active SCUT network.
